ask: Why is it on the path?
cards: The fibre that named a road and moved ideas along with cloth.
Gold north, salt south: the caravans that made Ghana, Mali and Songhai.
The monsoon exchange that linked Africa, Arabia, India and China long before Europeans arrived.
Cloves and pepper: small cargoes worth fortunes, and the wars fought to corner them.
The middleman city that grew rich on the eastern trade and fought to keep it.
The joint-stock company with a flag, an army and an empire of its own.
The bank at the heart of the first modern financial centre.
